title: Who Owns That? Evaluating Ownership Intuitions in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.39483v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Ownership establishes rights over the use, control, and transfer of objects. Understanding these relations is essential for AI systems to interact appropriately with people and their resources. Yet how large language models (LLMs) attribute ownership under competing claims remains unclear. We introduce the Competing Ownership Attribution Task (COAT), comprising 42 scenarios, and compare ownership allocations from 24 LLM configurations with those of 108 human participants. Overall, human-model similarity is close to human-human similarity, but models show greater homogeneity in their ownership judgments. Within individual answers, models also divide ownership more evenly among claimants than humans do. Pooling responses across model configurations reveals more scenarios with a shared judgment and fewer with distinct viewpoint groups than in humans. When humans form distinct groups, models may converge on one viewpoint or between competing

translated_title: 那是谁的？评估大型语言模型中的所有权直觉
translated_abstract: 所有权确立了人们对物品的使用、控制和转让权利。理解这些关系对于AI系统与人类及其资源进行恰当互动至关重要。然而，大型语言模型（LLM）在存在竞争性主张时如何归属所有权仍不清楚。我们引入了竞争性所有权归属任务（COAT），包含42个场景，并将24个LLM配置的所有权分配结果与108名人类参与者的结果进行比较。总体而言，人类与模型之间的相似度接近于人类与人类之间的相似度，但模型在所有权判断上表现出更大的同质性。在单个回答中，模型也比人类更均匀地在各主张者之间分配所有权。汇总跨模型配置的回应后发现，与人类相比，模型达成共同判断的场景更多，而形成不同观点群体的场景更少。当人类形成明显不同的群体时，模型可能会收敛于某一个观点，或介于相互竞争的观点之间。
tldr: 该研究提出了包含42个场景的竞争性所有权归属任务（COAT），发现大语言模型的所有权判断与人类整体相似，但模型内部更加同质化，且在竞争性主张之间分配所有权时比人类更均匀，缺乏人类那样的观点分化。
en_tdlr: This study introduces the Competing Ownership Attribution Task (COAT) with 42 scenarios and finds that while LLMs' ownership judgments are broadly similar to humans' overall, models are more internally homogeneous and distribute ownership more evenly among competing claimants, lacking the distinct viewpoint groups observed in human judgments.
